committed_turns.public_event: A newcomer has reached the card room.
committed_turns.spoken:
Narrator: A coin rings off the table edge and wobbles across the floor toward the south door, and nobody at the card table moves to catch it. Four of them sit at a worn table near that door, pale as candle tallow, pointed teeth showing when they breathe, dressed in lace and velvet gone shiny at the elbows. Each has coins stacked in front of them; a silver ring sits among the stacks in the middle. The man dealing has stopped mid-hand, one card pinned between two fingers. Beyond them, the whole north wall is a carved mountain, tiny dwarves in tiny caverns, stone sunbeams fanning over a long tub sunk into the floor.
Narrator: When the dealer speaks it is slow and savoring, each word laid down like a card he means you to look at.
Dealer: Well, now. The door brought us company. Come in, come in, the passage is draftier than we are. That coin by your boot is the most interesting thing that has happened at this table in an hour, so tell me: are you the sort who picks it up, or the sort who waits to see whose it is?

appraisal.label: interest

improv_read.connection: The gang works newcomers here; the dealer wants control of the encounter from the first word, so he speaks first and sets the terms of attention, not money.
improv_read.kit_choice: Let the room open on the dealer performing for an audience, and stay out of it herself so the player meets people, not a DM.

committed_turns.player_input: Evening, all! Didn't expect a card game this far down. I'll leave the coin for whoever owns it. So what's going on in here?
committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "Evening, all! Didn't expect a card game this far down. I'll leave the coin for whoever owns it. So what's going on in here?"
committed_turns.spoken:
Narrator: Under the table a velvet slipper stretches out, finds the coin, and drags it back into the shadows without its owner looking up from their cards. The dealer's card turns once between his fingers, face still hidden.
Dealer: The sort who waits. I had a feeling. What's going on, friend, is a quiet game among old acquaintances in the one room down here without anything trying to eat you. Nothing that needs explaining to someone who is only passing through. But nobody who says evening that nicely is only passing through, are they? What brings you all the way down to us?

appraisal.cause: The newcomer passes on the coin test politely and asks openly what the game is.
appraisal.label: interest

improv_read.connection: A courteous visitor gives the dealer nothing to push against; to keep control he has to read her, so he answers and fishes.
improv_read.kit_choice: A warm open question deserves a full answer from the people in the room; Kit has nothing to add and stays behind them.
improv_read.player_bid: Greets the table warmly, declines to pick up the coin, and asks what is going on.

committed_turns.player_input: Ha! Maybe not. I'm Wren. Honestly, I'm new down here and still getting my bearings. Is this your place?
committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "Ha! Maybe not. I'm Wren. Honestly, I'm new down here and still getting my bearings. Is this your place?"
committed_turns.spoken:
Dealer: Mine? Down here, a room belongs to whoever is sitting when the argument starts, Wren, and I am always sitting. New and getting your bearings. Then here is a bearing, free of charge: the chair on my left faces the door, which is where newcomers like to keep an eye. Sit, play a hand for coppers, and I will tell you which way is up. Directions cost something everywhere; I only ask that mine be paid in company.
Narrator: The player nearest the door, without a word, slides a short stack of coppers an inch toward the empty chair, the way you set out bread for a bird.

appraisal.cause: Wren gives a name and admits being new, which hands the dealer exactly the read he wants.
appraisal.label: interest

improv_read.connection: Admitting she is new marks her as a potential customer or mark; he claims ownership of the room because he wants to be the one in charge, and invites her to sit.
improv_read.kit_choice: The admission is the hook; Kit lets the dealer take it and lets a card player show the table has done this before.
improv_read.player_bid: Introduces herself as Wren, admits being new and lost, and asks whether this is his place.

public_brief.player_opening: Wren can sit, ask what the directions cost, or keep standing.
public_brief.tactic: Claim the room as his, then offer a seat and friendly directions that come with an implied price.

committed_turns.player_input: Alright, I'll sit for one hand, coppers only. But first, what do people usually lose at your table?
committed_turns.public_event: You declare: "Alright, I'll sit for one hand, coppers only. But first, what do people usually lose at your table?"
committed_turns.spoken:
Kit: One hand, coppers only. I am writing that down, because he is about to test it.
Dealer: What do they lose? Mostly their patience. Sometimes their boots. Once, a very stubborn dwarf lost an argument with that tub, but that is a longer story. Coppers it is, Wren. Two cards, face down, and one for luck.
Narrator: Cards hiss across the worn wood. As the last one lands, his little finger nudges the silver ring out of the pile and into the lamplight, where it sits between you like a question.
Dealer: Coppers buy you a seat. That buys you a story. Look at your cards whenever you like.

appraisal.cause: Wren sets a stake limit out loud before sitting, then asks what people lose.
appraisal.label: amusement

improv_read.connection: She has capped the risk; the dealer wants control, so he answers with a joke and immediately tests whether the cap holds by showing her the bigger pot.
improv_read.kit_choice: Kit holds the player to the stake she named, because a limit set aloud is part of the fiction and the dealer will test it.
improv_read.player_bid: Agrees to sit for one hand at copper stakes only, and asks what people usually lose here.
